title: Primitive symbolic Euler data are not trace-class summable
label: thm:primitive-symbolic-exclusion
text_start: Let \(A\) be a primitive adjacency matrix for a finite one-sided subshift of finite type. Put \(a_n(A)=\Tr(A^n)\), and let \[ p_n(A)=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{d\mid n}\mu(d)\,a_{n/d}(A) \] be the primitive-orbit counts; equivalently, \begin{equation} a_n(A)=\sum_{d\mid n}d\,p_d(A). \end{equation} Then, for the Perron root \(\lambda\) of \(A\), \[ \zeta_A(z) :=\exp\!\left(\sum_{n\ge 1}\frac{a_n(A)}{n}z^n\right) =\det(I-zA)^{-1} =\prod_{n\ge 1}(1-z^n)^{-p_n(A)} \] for every \(|z|<\lambda^{-1}\). The Euler product identity is an equality of holomorphic germs at \(z=0\); equivalently, it is an identity of formal power series. Moreover, \[ \sum_{n\ge1} n\,p_n(A)<\infty \qquad\Longleftrightarrow\qquad A=[1]. \]

title: Role of the symbolic product
label: rem:symbolic-product-role
text_start: For primitive finite matrices, the numbers \(p_n(A)\) are non-negative integers because they count primitive periodic orbits. This arithmetic feature belongs to the finite-state category. The proposition shows that, except for the one-symbol fixed-point shift, the primitive symbolic Euler product \[ \prod_{n\ge1}(1-z^n)^{-p_n(A)} \] is used in this paper only as a germ-level motivation and not as a summable cyclic zero divisor for \Cref{thm:cyclic-fredholm-realisation}. For instance, for the full \(k\)-shift with \(k\ge2\), \(a_n(A)=k^n\), \(\zeta_A(z)=(1-kz)^{-1}\), and \(\sum_n n\,p_n(A)=\infty\).

title: Connecting Fredholm--Witt identity
label: prop:fredholm-witt-bridge
text_start: The following is a direct consequence of the classical Fredholm determinant identity; we record it here to fix notation and to make the Euler-product structure explicit. For every trace-class operator \(T\) and every \(\abs{z}<\min(1,\norm{T}^{-1})\), with the convention \(\norm{0}^{-1}:=\infty\), \[ \det(I-zT)^{-1} =\exp\!\left(\sum_{n\ge 1}\frac{a_n(T)}{n}z^n\right) =\prod_{n\ge 1}(1-z^n)^{-p_n(T)}, \] where \(\log(1-z^m)\) denotes the principal branch on \(\abs{z}<1\). This identity holds as an equality of holomorphic germs at \(z=0\); equivalently, it is an identity of formal power series. The exponents \(p_n(T)\) are in general not integers, so the Euler product on the right is not a finite collection of zero-free factors, and the expression should not be extended beyond the common disc of convergence without an explicit branch choice.

title: Arithmetic flexibility
label: rem:witt-arithmetic-flexibility
text_start: In the finite-state setting of \Cref{thm:primitive-symbolic-exclusion}, the corresponding coordinates count primitive periodic orbits and are non-negative integers. For a general trace-class operator, the coordinates \(p_n(T)\) need neither be integers nor be non-negative. Thus trace-class realisability is strictly broader than finite-state realisability.

title: Witt coordinates are not cyclic divisor multiplicities
label: rem:witt-versus-cyclic-data
text_start: For a trace-class operator \(T\), \Cref{prop:fredholm-witt-bridge} associates the Witt coordinates \[ p_n(T)=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{d\mid n}\mu(d)\,\Tr(T^{n/d}) \qquad (n\ge1). \] These are complex numbers extracted from the trace sequence of \(T\). By contrast, the realisation problem in \Cref{sec:fredholm} later fixes discrete cyclic zero-divisor data \[ \mathcal D=\{(n_j,\beta_j,m_j)\}_{j\in J}, \qquad m_j\in\NN,\ \beta_j\in\CC\setminus\{0\}, \] describing prescribed factors \((1-\beta_j z^{n_j})^{m_j}\) in a Fredholm determinant. In general there is no identification \(p_n(T)=m_n\), nor do the \(p_n(T)\) recover the triples \((n_j,\beta_j,m_j)\). The only overlap is the special integral unit-root case recorded in \Cref{prop:cyclic-witt-compatibility}. title: Compatibility of cyclic zero divisors with Witt coordinates
label: prop:cyclic-witt-compatibility
text_start: Let \(\mathcal D=\{(n_j,\beta_j,m_j)\}_{j\in J}\) satisfy \[ n_j,m_j\in\NN,\qquad \beta_j\in\CC\setminus\{0\},\qquad \sum_{j\in J}m_j n_j\abs{\beta_j}^{1/n_j}<\infty, \] and let \(L_{\mathcal D}\) be the cyclic model from \Cref{lem:cyclic-product-trace-norm-limit}. Then for every \(n\ge1\), \[ a_n(L_{\mathcal D}) =\sum_{\{j\in J:n_j\mid n\}} n_jm_j\,\beta_j^{n/n_j}, \] and therefore \[ p_n(L_{\mathcal D}) =\frac{1}{n}\sum_{d\mid n}\mu(d) \sum_{\{j\in J:n_j\mid n/d\}} n_jm_j\,\beta_j^{(n/d)/n_j}. \] In particular, the Witt coordinates are determined by the cyclic zero-divisor data, but they are generally complex and need not equal the multiplicities \(m_j\). In the special unit-root case \[ \mathcal D=\{(n,1,m_n)\}_{n\ge1}, \qquad \sum_{n\ge1} n\,m_n<\infty, \] one has \[ a_n(L_{\mathcal D})=\sum_{d\mid n} d\,m_d, \qquad p_n(L_{\mathcal D})=m_n. \] Thus the cyclic-block theorem below is a

title: Cyclic data, trace budget, and support size
label: def:cyclic-data-trace-budget
text_start: A countable cyclic datum is a family \[ \mathcal D=\{(n_j,\beta_j,m_j)\}_{j\in J}, \qquad n_j,m_j\in\NN,\quad \beta_j\in\CC\setminus\{0\}, \] indexed by a finite or countably infinite set \(J\). Its trace budget, formal positive determinant, and numerical support size are \[ \tau_{\mathcal D} :=\sum_{j\in J}m_j n_j\abs{\beta_j}^{1/n_j}\in[0,\infty], \] \[ D_{\mathcal D}(z) :=\prod_{j\in J}(1-\beta_jz^{n_j})^{m_j}, \qquad N_{\mathcal D}:=\sum_{j\in J}m_jn_j\in\NN\cup\{\infty\}. \] The associated cyclic zero divisor is the divisor on \(\CC^\times\) \[ Z_{\mathcal D} :=\sum_{j\in J}m_j\sum_{\lambda^{n_j}=\beta_j}[\lambda]. \] Thus a point \(\lambda\in\CC^\times\) has divisor multiplicity \[ M_{\mathcal D}(\lambda) :=\sum_{\{j\in J:\lambda^{n_j}=\beta_j\}}m_j, \] possibly \(+\infty\) before summability or realisability hypotheses are imposed. title: Single cyclic-block spectrum
label: lem:single-cyclic-block-spectrum
text_start: Let \(n,m\in\NN\), \(\beta\in\CC\setminus\{0\}\), and \(\alpha^n=\beta\). Then the non-zero eigenvalues of \(C(n,\alpha)\otimes I_m\) are \[ \alpha\omega,\qquad \omega^n=1, \] each with multiplicity \(m\), and \[ \det\!\bigl(I-z(C(n,\alpha)\otimes I_m)\bigr) =(1-\beta z^n)^m . \]

title: Finite cyclic truncation determinant with positive exponents
label: lem:finite-cyclic-truncation-determinant
text_start: Let \(F\) be a finite set of indices and put \[ L_F:=\bigoplus_{j\in F}\bigl(C(n_j,\alpha_j)\otimes I_{m_j}\bigr), \qquad \alpha_j^{n_j}=\beta_j. \] Then, as a finite-dimensional determinant identity, \[ \det(I-zL_F) =\prod_{j\in F}(1-\beta_j z^{n_j})^{m_j}, \qquad \det(I-zL_F)^{-1} =\prod_{j\in F}(1-\beta_j z^{n_j})^{-m_j} \] wherever the reciprocal is defined.

title: Direct normal convergence of the cyclic product
label: lem:direct-cyclic-weierstrass-product
text_start: Assume \[ \sum_{j\in J}m_j n_j\abs{\beta_j}^{1/n_j}<\infty, \qquad a_j:=\abs{\beta_j}^{1/n_j}. \] Then for every \(R>0\), \[ \sum_{j\in J} m_j \sup_{\abs z\le R}\abs{\beta_j z^{n_j}} \le \sum_{j\in J}m_j\abs{\beta_j}R^{n_j} =\sum_{j\in J}m_j(Ra_j)^{n_j} <\infty. \] Consequently the infinite product \[ \prod_{j\in J}(1-\beta_j z^{n_j})^{m_j} \] converges normally on compact subsets of \(\CC\). In particular it converges locally uniformly, defines an entire function, and its value is independent of the enumeration of \(J\).

title: Trace-norm limit convention for cyclic products
label: lem:cyclic-product-trace-norm-limit
text_start: Assume \[ \sum_{j\in J}m_j n_j\abs{\beta_j}^{1/n_j}<\infty \] and choose \(\alpha_j^{n_j}=\beta_j\). Let \[ H_{\mathcal D} :=\bigoplus_{j\in J}\bigl(\CC^{n_j}\otimes\CC^{m_j}\bigr), \qquad L_{\mathcal D} :=\bigoplus_{j\in J}\bigl(C(n_j,\alpha_j)\otimes I_{m_j}\bigr) \] on \(H_{\mathcal D}\), and let \(L_{\mathcal D}^{(N)}\) be any finite truncation along an enumeration of \(J\). Then \(L_{\mathcal D}^{(N)}\to L_{\mathcal D}\) in trace norm and \[ \prod_{j\in J}(1-\beta_j z^{n_j})^{m_j} =\lim_{N\to\infty} \prod_{j\le N}(1-\beta_j z^{n_j})^{m_j} \] locally uniformly for \(z\in\CC\), and \[ \det(I-zL_{\mathcal D}) =\lim_{N\to\infty} \prod_{j\le N}(1-\beta_j z^{n_j})^{m_j} \] locally uniformly for \(z\in\CC\). On any connected zero-free neighbourhood \(\Omega\ni0\) for this determinant, \[ \det(I-zL_{\mathcal D})^{-1} =\lim_{N\to\infty} \prod_{j\le N}(1-\beta_j z^{n_j})^{-m_j} \] locally uni

title: Choice of roots and unitary relabelling
label: lem:choice-of-roots
text_start: Let \(n,m\in\NN\), let \(\beta\in\CC\setminus\{0\}\), and let \(\alpha^n=(\alpha')^n=\beta\). Then \(C(n,\alpha)\otimes I_m\) and \(C(n,\alpha')\otimes I_m\) are unitarily equivalent. More explicitly, if \(\eta:=\alpha'/\alpha\), so that \(\eta^n=1\), and \((e_0,\dots,e_{n-1})\) is the cyclic basis in which \(\Pi_n e_k=e_{k+1\!\!\pmod n}\), then \[ U_\eta e_k:=\eta^k e_k \qquad (0\le k<n) \] defines a unitary on \(\CC^n\) satisfying \[ U_\eta C(n,\alpha)U_\eta^{-1}=C(n,\alpha'). \] Consequently any two root choices in the construction of \(L_{\mathcal D}\) give unitarily equivalent cyclic models, via the block direct sum of the maps \(U_{\eta_j}\otimes I_{m_j}\). The determinant data therefore determine the cyclic model only up to this explicit relabelling and the addition of zero summands.

title: Acyclic construction interface for cyclic data
label: prop:cyclic-data-construction-interface
text_start: Let \(\mathcal D\) be a countable cyclic datum in the sense of \Cref{def:cyclic-data-trace-budget} with \(\tau_{\mathcal D}<\infty\), and choose roots \(\alpha_j^{n_j}=\beta_j\). For each finite \(F\Subset J\), set \[ H_F:=\bigoplus_{j\in F}(\CC^{n_j}\otimes\CC^{m_j}), \qquad L_F:=\bigoplus_{j\in F}(C(n_j,\alpha_j)\otimes I_{m_j}), \] and regard \(L_F\) as acting by zero on the orthogonal complement of \(H_F\) in \(H_{\mathcal D}\). Then the net \((L_F)_{F\Subset J}\), directed by inclusion, converges unconditionally in trace norm to a normal operator \(L_{\mathcal D}\in\sone(H_{\mathcal D})\). This limit satisfies \[ \norm{L_{\mathcal D}}_1=\tau_{\mathcal D}, \qquad \dim H_{\mathcal D}= \begin{cases} N_{\mathcal D},& J\text{ finite},\\ \aleph_0,& J\text{ infinite}, \end{cases} \] where the second equality is a Hilbert-space dimension identity. Moreover \(D_{\mathcal D}\) is an entire fu

title: Closed non-zero spectral support
label: def:closed-nonzero-support
text_start: For a normal trace-class operator \(L\), write \[ \mathsf S(L):= \overline{\mathrm{span}} \{\,\ker(L-\lambda I):\lambda\in\spec(L)\setminus\{0\}\,\}. \] This notation is the support convention used throughout the normal construction and classification sections; the model-specific range formula is recorded later in \Cref{lem:cyclic-sum-range-closure}.

title: Closed support is \(\overline{\Ran L}\)
label: lem:normal-support-range-closure
text_start: If \(L\) is normal and trace-class, then \[ \mathsf S(L)=(\ker L)^\perp=\overline{\Ran(L)}. \] This identifies the closed support with \(\overline{\Ran L}\). It does not assert that \(\Ran L\) is closed.

title: Sharp trace-norm budget for cyclic zero divisors
label: prop:sharp-trace-budget-support-obstruction
text_start: Let \(\mathcal D=\{(n_j,\beta_j,m_j)\}_{j\in J}\) be a countable family with \(n_j,m_j\in\NN\) and \(\beta_j\in\CC\setminus\{0\}\). Choose roots \(\alpha_j^{n_j}=\beta_j\), and let \[ \Lambda_{\mathcal D} := \bigl\{\!\bigl\{\alpha_j\omega: j\in J,\ \omega^{n_j}=1,\text{ repeated }m_j\text{ times} \bigr\}\!\bigr\} \] be the prescribed non-zero spectral multiset, with multiplicities added when the same complex number occurs more than once. Suppose \(L\in\sone(H)\) is normal and its non-zero spectrum, counted with algebraic multiplicity, is exactly \(\Lambda_{\mathcal D}\). Then the trace-norm budget is forced: \[ \|L\|_1 = \sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda_{\mathcal D}}\abs{\lambda} = \sum_{j\in J}m_j n_j\abs{\beta_j}^{1/n_j} <\infty . \] Moreover \[ \dim \mathsf S(L)= \begin{cases} N_{\mathcal D},& J\text{ finite},\\ \aleph_0,& J\text{ infinite}, \end{cases} \] as a Hilbert-space dimension; equival

title: Collapsed spectral multiplicities of Euler data
label: prop:collapsed-spectral-multiplicities
text_start: Let \(\mathcal D=\{(n_j,\beta_j,m_j)\}_{j\in J}\) satisfy \[ n_j,m_j\in\NN,\qquad \beta_j\in\CC\setminus\{0\},\qquad \sum_{j\in J}m_j n_j\abs{\beta_j}^{1/n_j}<\infty, \] and choose roots \(\alpha_j^{n_j}=\beta_j\). title: Regularized determinant normalization
label: def:regularized-determinant-normalization
text_start: For an integer \(r\ge1\) and a finite-dimensional operator \(A\), this paper uses \[ \det_r(I-zA) := \det(I-zA) \exp\!\left(\sum_{q=1}^{r-1}\frac{z^q}{q}\operatorname{tr}(A^q)\right), \] with the empty sum interpreted as \(0\) when \(r=1\). For \(A\in\mathcal S_r\) on a Hilbert space, \(\det_r(I-zA)\) is the locally uniform limit of this expression along finite-rank approximants in \(\mathcal S_r\), equivalently the standard regularized Fredholm determinant of order \(r\) \cite[Chapter~9]{Simon2005TraceIdeals}. In particular \(\det_1(I-zA)=\det(I-zA)\) on trace-class operators, and for a finite cyclic block satisfying \(B^n=\beta I\), \[ \det_r(I-zB) =(1-\beta z^n) \exp\!\left(\sum_{1\le q\le (r-1)/n} \frac{\beta^q z^{qn}}{q}\right). \]

title: Regularized zero-divisor chain for cyclic blocks
label: prop:regularized-zero-divisor-chain
text_start: Let \(r\ge1\), let \(\mathcal D=\{(n_j,\beta_j,m_j)\}_{j\in J}\) satisfy \[ \sum_{j\in J}m_jn_j\abs{\beta_j}^{p/n_j}<\infty \] for some \(1<p\le r\), and let \(P_F^{(r)}\) be the finite-subset products determined by \Cref{def:regularized-determinant-normalization}. Then, for every finite \(F\Subset J\), the zero divisor of \(P_F^{(r)} \) on \(\CC\) is \[ \sum_{j\in F}m_j\sum_{\lambda^{n_j}=\beta_j}[\lambda^{-1}], \] and the locally uniform limit supplied by \Cref{lem:regularized-cyclic-finite-subset-products} has finite zero order at \(z=\lambda^{-1}\) equal to \[ M_{\mathcal D}(\lambda) =\sum_{\{j\in J:\lambda^{n_j}=\beta_j\}}m_j \] for every \(\lambda\in\CC^\times\). title: Finite-subset convention for regularized cyclic products
label: lem:regularized-cyclic-finite-subset-products
text_start: Let \(1<p\le r\) with \(r\in\NN\), and let \(\mathcal D=\{(n_j,\beta_j,m_j)\}_{j\in J}\) satisfy \[ \sum_{j\in J}m_jn_j\abs{\beta_j}^{p/n_j}<\infty. \] For \(F\Subset J\), define \[ P_F^{(r)}(z):= \prod_{j\in F}(1-\beta_jz^{n_j})^{m_j} \exp\!\left( m_j\sum_{1\le q\le (r-1)/n_j} \frac{\beta_j^qz^{qn_j}}{q} \right). \] Then \(P_F^{(r)}\) converges locally uniformly on \(\CC\), as \(F\Subset J\), to an entire function independent of the enumeration of \(J\). More precisely, for every \(R>0\), all but finitely many indices satisfy \(R\abs{\beta_j}^{1/n_j}\le1/2\), and for such \(j\) and \(\abs z\le R\), \[ \left| \log\!\left[ (1-\beta_jz^{n_j})^{m_j} \exp\!\left( m_j\sum_{1\le q\le (r-1)/n_j} \frac{\beta_j^qz^{qn_j}}{q} \right) \right] \right| \le C_{p,r,R}\,m_jn_j\abs{\beta_j}^{p/n_j}. \]

title: Exact Schatten membership threshold for the cyclic model
label: thm:schatten-cyclic-model-membership
text_start: Let \(1<p<\infty\), let \(r=\lceil p\rceil\), and let \(\mathcal D=\{(n_j,\beta_j,m_j)\}_{j\in J}\) be countable cyclic data. The integer \(r\) is recorded only for the later regularized determinant statement; the present theorem classifies membership of the cyclic model in the smaller class \(\mathcal S_p\), not existence or uniqueness of \(\det_r\) on its natural domain \(\mathcal S_r\). Choose roots \(\alpha_j^{n_j}=\beta_j\), and form the cyclic direct sum \(L_{\mathcal D}=\bigoplus_j(C(n_j,\alpha_j)\otimes I_{m_j})\) whenever it is defined as a compact operator. Then \[ L_{\mathcal D}\in\mathcal S_p \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \sum_{j\in J}m_jn_j\abs{\beta_j}^{p/n_j}<\infty, \] and in this case \[ \norm{L_{\mathcal D}}_p^p =\sum_{j\in J}m_jn_j\abs{\beta_j}^{p/n_j}. \]

title: Regularized cyclic determinant and the \(\mathcal S_p\) lower bound
label: thm:schatten-cyclic-regularized-determinant
text_start: Let \(1<p<\infty\), let \(r=\lceil p\rceil\), and let \(\mathcal D=\{(n_j,\beta_j,m_j)\}_{j\in J}\) be countable cyclic data satisfying \[ \tau_{\mathcal D,p} :=\sum_{j\in J}m_jn_j\abs{\beta_j}^{p/n_j}<\infty . \] Choose roots \(\alpha_j^{n_j}=\beta_j\), and let \(L_{\mathcal D}\) be the cyclic model from \Cref{thm:schatten-cyclic-model-membership}. title: Controlled scope of the regularized cyclic package
label: cor:regularized-controlled-extension-scope
text_start: Let \(1<p<\infty\), put \(r=\lceil p\rceil\), and let \(\mathcal D\) be countable cyclic data satisfying \[ \sum_{j\in J}m_jn_j\abs{\beta_j}^{p/n_j}<\infty . \] Then the regularized product formula of \Cref{thm:schatten-cyclic-regularized-determinant} is a controlled extension of the trace-class Fredholm determinant realization theorem in the following precise sense. \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}] \item It first asserts the smaller-budget membership \(L_{\mathcal D}\in\mathcal S_p\) and computes \(\det_r(I-zL_{\mathcal D})\) for that model. \item Its converse lower bound applies only to operators \(T\in\mathcal S_p\) whose regularized determinant is obtained as the locally uniform prescribed cyclic product limit appearing in the theorem. \item It does not assert that every operator in the natural \(\mathcal S_r\)-domain of \(\det_r\), or every possible \(\det_r\)-zero diviso

title: Regularized determinant domain boundary
label: prop:regularized-domain-boundary
text_start: Let \(1<p<\infty\), put \(r=\lceil p\rceil\), and let \(\mathcal D\) be cyclic data satisfying \[ \sum_{j\in J}m_jn_j\abs{\beta_j}^{p/n_j}<\infty . \] The conclusions of \Cref{thm:schatten-cyclic-regularized-determinant} are conclusions in the smaller Schatten class \(\mathcal S_p\): they give membership of the normal cyclic model in \(\mathcal S_p\), the explicit \(\det_r\)-factorization for that model, and the sharp lower bound for \(\mathcal S_p\)-operators whose regularized determinant has the prescribed cyclic product limit. They do not classify all operators in the natural determinant domain \(\mathcal S_r\). More precisely, whenever \(p<r\) there are cyclic data for which \[ \sum_jm_jn_j\abs{\beta_j}^{r/n_j}<\infty, \qquad \sum_jm_jn_j\abs{\beta_j}^{p/n_j}=\infty . \] For those data the normal cyclic model belongs to \(\mathcal S_r\), and hence has a well-defined \(\det_r\), but i

title: Fredholm and regularized zero-divisor correspondence
label: prop:fredholm-regularized-zero-divisor-correspondence
text_start: Let \(r\in\NN\). If \(T\in\mathcal S_r(H)\), then \(z\mapsto\det_r(I-zT)\) is an entire function with value \(1\) at \(z=0\), and its zero divisor is \[ \sum_{\lambda\in\sigma(T)\setminus\{0\}} m_{\mathrm{alg}}(\lambda;T)\,[\lambda^{-1}], \] where \(m_{\mathrm{alg}}(\lambda;T)\) denotes algebraic multiplicity. Thus the order of the zero at \(z=\lambda^{-1}\) is exactly \(m_{\mathrm{alg}}(\lambda;T)\), and there are no other zeros. For \(r=1\), this is the ordinary Fredholm determinant; in particular \[ \det(I-zT) =\prod_{\lambda\in\sigma(T)\setminus\{0\}} (1-z\lambda)^{m_{\mathrm{alg}}(\lambda;T)} \] locally uniformly on compact subsets of \(\CC\). Consequently, if a trace-class operator \(Q\) is quasinilpotent, then \(\det(I-zQ)\equiv1\). If a Schatten-\(r\) operator \(Q\) is quasinilpotent, then \(\det_r(I-zQ)\equiv1\).

title: Classical Fredholm determinant rigidity
label: lem:fredholm-spectral-rigidity
text_start: Let \(T_1,T_2\in \sone\). If \[ \det(I-zT_1)=\det(I-zT_2) \] in a neighbourhood of \(z=0\), then the non-zero spectra of \(T_1\) and \(T_2\) coincide with algebraic multiplicity. Consequently, \[ \Tr(T_1^n)=\Tr(T_2^n), \qquad p_n(T_1)=p_n(T_2) \qquad (n\ge 1). \]

title: Product-side divisor multiplicity
label: lem:product-side-cyclic-divisor-multiplicity
text_start: Let \[ \mathcal D=\{(n_j,\beta_j,m_j)\}_{j\in J} \] be countable cyclic data and define \[ P_F(z):=\prod_{j\in F}(1-\beta_jz^{n_j})^{m_j}, \qquad F\Subset J. \] Suppose \(T\in\sone(H)\) and the net \((P_F)_{F\Subset J}\), directed by inclusion, converges locally uniformly on \(\CC\) to \(\det(I-zT)\). Then, for every \(\lambda\in\CC^\times\), \[ M_{\mathcal D}(\lambda) :=\sum_{\{j\in J:\lambda^{n_j}=\beta_j\}}m_j \] is finite and is at most the algebraic multiplicity of \(\lambda\) as an eigenvalue of \(T\).

title: Exact trace-class threshold and forced root budget
label: thm:normal-realizability-threshold
text_start: Let \(\mathcal D=\{(n_j,\beta_j,m_j)\}_{j\in J}\) be a countable family with \[ n_j,m_j\in\NN,\qquad \beta_j\in\CC\setminus\{0\}. \] For a trace-class operator \(A\), the assertion \[ \det(I-zA)=\prod_{j\in J}(1-\beta_j z^{n_j})^{m_j} \] means the following product-side condition. The finite products \[ P_F(z):=\prod_{j\in F}(1-\beta_j z^{n_j})^{m_j}, \qquad F\Subset J, \] directed by inclusion, converge locally uniformly on compact subsets of \(\CC\) to the Fredholm determinant \(\det(I-zA)\). No summability of the root budget is assumed in this convention; the theorem asserts that such a Fredholm-determinant limit exists exactly in the summable case. title: Collapsed-multiset normal realisation and determinant classification
label: thm:collapsed-multiset-normal-realisation
text_start: Let \(M:\CC^\times\to\NN\cup\{0\}\) have countable support \[ \Sigma_M:=\{\lambda\in\CC^\times:M(\lambda)\neq0\} \] and satisfy \[ \tau_M:=\sum_{\lambda\in\Sigma_M}\abs{\lambda}M(\lambda)<\infty. \] Put \[ H_M:=\bigoplus_{\lambda\in\Sigma_M}\CC^{M(\lambda)}, \qquad N_M:=\bigoplus_{\lambda\in\Sigma_M}\lambda I_{M(\lambda)} \] on \(H_M\). Then \(N_M\) is normal trace class, \[ \norm{N_M}_1=\tau_M, \] and the finite-subset products \[ D_{M,F}(z):=\prod_{\lambda\in F}(1-\lambda z)^{M(\lambda)}, \qquad F\Subset\Sigma_M, \] converge locally uniformly on \(\CC\) to an entire function \[ D_M(z):=\prod_{\lambda\in\Sigma_M}(1-\lambda z)^{M(\lambda)} =\det(I-zN_M). \] Moreover, if \(L\in\sone(H)\) is normal, then \[ \det(I-zL)=D_M(z) \] as a holomorphic germ at \(0\) if and only if there exist a Hilbert space \(H_0\) and a unitary \(U:H\to H_0\oplus H_M\) such that \[ ULU^{-1}=0_{H_0}\oplus N_M . \

title: Intrinsic normal trace-class realisability criterion
label: cor:arbitrary-collapsed-multiset-normal-realisation
text_start: Let \(M:\CC^\times\to\NN\cup\{0\}\) have countable support. title: Cyclic-block realisation of prescribed cyclic zero divisors and normal classification
label: thm:cyclic-fredholm-realisation
text_start: Let \(\mathcal D=\{(n_j,\beta_j,m_j)\}_{j\in J}\) be a countable family with \[ n_j,m_j\in\NN,\qquad \beta_j\in\CC\setminus\{0\}, \] and assume that \[ \sum_{j\in J}m_j n_j\abs{\beta_j}^{1/n_j}<\infty. \] Choose \(\alpha_j\in\CC\) with \(\alpha_j^{n_j}=\beta_j\), and set \[ H_{\mathcal D} :=\bigoplus_{j\in J}\bigl(\CC^{n_j}\otimes\CC^{m_j}\bigr), \qquad L_{\mathcal D} :=\bigoplus_{j\in J}\bigl(C(n_j,\alpha_j)\otimes I_{m_j}\bigr). \] Then \(L_{\mathcal D}\in \sone(H_{\mathcal D})\) is normal, and the entire Fredholm determinant \[ D_{\mathcal D}(z):=\det(I-zL_{\mathcal D}) \] satisfies \[ D_{\mathcal D}(z) =\prod_{j\in J}(1-\beta_j z^{n_j})^{m_j} \] locally uniformly on compact subsets of \(\CC\), where the right-hand side is the limit of the positive-exponent finite truncation determinants. title: Block-cyclic normal realisation
label: def:block-cyclic-normal-realisation
text_start: A normal operator \(L\in \sone(H)\) satisfying \Cref{thm:cyclic-fredholm-realisation}\textup{(ii)} is called a block-cyclic normal realisation of the Euler data \(\mathcal D=\{(n_j,\beta_j,m_j)\}_{j\in J}\). This definition records only the unitary normal form of the non-zero spectral part. It includes no assertion that \(\Ran L\) is the whole cyclic-block space; that range \(\Ran L\) is the separate object computed in \Cref{lem:cyclic-sum-range-closure}.

title: Algebraic range and closed support of a cyclic direct sum
label: lem:cyclic-sum-range-closure
text_start: This lemma uses the support convention of \Cref{def:closed-nonzero-support}: closed support means \(\mathsf S(L)=\overline{\Ran L}\) for normal trace-class \(L\), while the algebraic range itself may be a proper dense subspace. title: Support, range, and trace budget of a block-cyclic realisation
label: cor:block-cyclic-rigidity
text_start: Let \(L\) be a block-cyclic normal realisation of \(\mathcal D\) in the sense of \Cref{def:block-cyclic-normal-realisation}. Let \(U:H\to H_0\oplus H_{\mathcal D}\) be any unitary representation with \(ULU^{-1}=0_{H_0}\oplus L_{\mathcal D}\), and write \(L_j=C(n_j,\alpha_j)\otimes I_{m_j}\). title: Sharpness of the summability condition
label: rem:summability-sharpness
text_start: \Cref{thm:normal-realizability-threshold} packages the exact ``if and only if'' statement: \[ \sum_{j\in J}m_j n_j\abs{\beta_j}^{1/n_j}<\infty \] is exactly the criterion for trace-class realisability of the prescribed Euler data, and hence in particular for trace-class normal realisability. The resulting closed support of the canonical normal model is then forced by \Cref{cor:block-cyclic-rigidity}. Thus the summability hypothesis is not merely sufficient but necessary.

title: Finite Euler products give finite-rank determinant models
label: cor:finite-rank-realisation
text_start: If \(J\) is finite in \Cref{thm:cyclic-fredholm-realisation}, then \(L_{\mathcal D}\) is finite-rank. As an immediate specialization, every finite reciprocal Euler product \[ \prod_{j=1}^N(1-\beta_j z^{n_j})^{-m_j} \] is realised in the determinant-side sense: there is a finite-rank normal operator \(L\) with \[ \det(I-zL)=\prod_{j=1}^N(1-\beta_j z^{n_j})^{m_j}, \] and the displayed reciprocal product is \(\det(I-zL)^{-1}\) wherever this determinant is non-zero. The non-zero rank of \(L\) is exactly \(\sum_{j=1}^N m_j n_j\).

title: Classical ordered Weyl--Ky Fan--Lidskii inequality
label: lem:weyl-ky-fan-trace-class
text_start: Let \(T\in\sone(H)\). Let \((\lambda_k(T))_{k\ge1}\) be the eigenvalues of \(T\), repeated according to algebraic multiplicity and ordered so that \[ \abs{\lambda_1(T)}\ge \abs{\lambda_2(T)}\ge \cdots, \] padding by zeros once the non-zero spectrum is exhausted. Let \((s_k(T))_{k\ge1}\) be the singular values of \(T\), ordered so that \[ s_1(T)\ge s_2(T)\ge \cdots \ge 0. \] Then for every \(N\ge1\), \[ \sum_{k=1}^N \abs{\lambda_k(T)} \le \sum_{k=1}^N s_k(T). \] Consequently, \[ \sum_{k\ge1}\abs{\lambda_k(T)}\le \|T\|_1. \]

title: Ordered non-zero root-space flag
label: lem:ordered-nonzero-root-flag
text_start: Let \(K\) be a compact operator on a separable Hilbert space, and let \((\mu_q)_{q\in Q}\), where \(Q=\{1,\ldots,m\}\) or \(Q=\NN\), be any ordering of the non-zero eigenvalues of \(K\), each repeated according to algebraic multiplicity. Then there is an increasing family \[ 0=E_0\subset E_1\subset E_2\subset\cdots \] of finite-dimensional \(K\)-invariant subspaces, indexed by \(q\in Q\), such that \(\dim E_q=q\) and the induced operator on \(E_q/E_{q-1}\) is multiplication by \(\mu_q\). If \(E:=\overline{\bigcup_q E_q}\), then \(E\) contains every non-zero Riesz root space of \(K\), and the compact operator induced by \(K\) on the quotient space \(H/E\) has no non-zero eigenvalues.

title: Classical Ringrose triangularisation in Schatten ideals
label: lem:ringrose-prescribed-diagonal
text_start: Let \(1\le p<\infty\) and let \(T\in\mathcal S_p(H)\). After replacing \(H\) by the reducing subspace \[ H_T:=\overline{\mathrm{span}}\{u_r,v_r:r\ge1\} \] coming from any singular-value expansion \(T=\sum_{r\ge1}s_r(T)\langle\,\cdot\,,u_r\rangle v_r\), the operator acts on a separable Hilbert space and vanishes on \(H_T^\perp\). On this separable reducing part there is an orthonormal basis \((e_k)_{k\ge1}\) in which the matrix of \(T\) is upper triangular. The non-zero diagonal entries may be chosen so that their non-zero subsequence occurs in any prescribed ordering of the non-zero eigenvalues of \(T\), each repeated according to algebraic multiplicity. Every other diagonal entry is zero. title: Two-by-two trace-norm pinching identity
label: lem:two-by-two-trace-norm-pinching
text_start: For \(a,b,c\in\CC\), let \[ B=\begin{pmatrix}a&c\\0&b\end{pmatrix}. \] Then \[ \|B\|_1^2=(\abs{a}+\abs{b})^2+\abs{c}^2. \] In particular, \[ \|B\|_1\ge \abs{a}+\abs{b}, \] and equality holds if and only if \(c=0\).

title: Two-by-two Schatten pinching rigidity
label: lem:two-by-two-schatten-pinching
text_start: Let \(1<p<\infty\). For \(a,b,c\in\CC\), put \[ B=\begin{pmatrix}a&c\\0&b\end{pmatrix} \] and define \[ \Phi_p(a,b,c):=\|B\|_p^p-\abs a^p-\abs b^p . \] Then \[ \Phi_p(a,b,c)\ge0, \] Equality holds if and only if \(c=0\). For fixed \(a,b\), if \[ \Phi_p(a,b,c_\nu)\longrightarrow0, \] then \(c_\nu\to0\).

title: Uniform two-by-two Schatten pinching modulus
label: lem:uniform-two-by-two-schatten-modulus
text_start: Let \(1<p<\infty\), let \(E\subset\CC\) be finite, and let \(R>0\). For \(a,b,c\in\CC\), set \[ B(a,b,c):=\begin{pmatrix}a&c\\0&b\end{pmatrix}, \qquad \Phi_p(a,b,c):=\|B(a,b,c)\|_p^p-\abs a^p-\abs b^p . \] Define \[ \Theta_{p,E,R}(\varepsilon) := \sup\{\abs c: a,b\in E, \|B(a,b,c)\|_p\le R, \Phi_p(a,b,c)\le\varepsilon\}, \] with the convention that the supremum of the empty set is \(0\). Then \(\Theta_{p,E,R}\) is a finite nondecreasing function on \([0,\infty)\) and \[ \Theta_{p,E,R}(\varepsilon)\downarrow0 \qquad(\varepsilon\downarrow0). \] Consequently, whenever \(a,b\in E\), \(\|B(a,b,c)\|_p\le R\), and \(\Phi_p(a,b,c)\le\varepsilon\), one has \(\abs c\le\Theta_{p,E,R}(\varepsilon)\).

title: Standard trace-norm convergence of Schur compressions
label: lem:trace-norm-schur-compressions

title: Standard Schatten-norm convergence of Schur compressions
label: lem:schatten-schur-compressions
text_start: Let \(1\le p<\infty\), let \(T\in\mathcal S_p(H)\), and let \((P_N)_{N\ge1}\) be finite-rank orthogonal projections with \(P_N\to I\) strongly. Then \[ P_NTP_N\longrightarrow T \qquad\text{in }\mathcal S_p\text{-norm}. \]

title: Two-by-two square-root sharpness
label: prop:two-by-two-square-root-sharpness
text_start: Fix \(\lambda\in\CC\setminus\{0\}\). For \(c\in\CC\), set \[ A_c=\begin{pmatrix}\lambda&c\\0&\lambda\end{pmatrix}. \] Then each \(A_c\) lies in the determinant fiber \[ \det(I-zA_c)=(1-\lambda z)^2, \] whose two-dimensional minimizer class is \(\{\lambda I_2\}\), and \[ \|A_c\|_1-2\abs\lambda = \frac{\abs c^2} {\sqrt{4\abs{\lambda}^2+\abs c^2}+2\abs{\lambda}} =\frac{\abs c^2}{4\abs\lambda}+O(\abs c^4). \] Moreover \[ \operatorname{dist}_1(A_c,\{\lambda I_2\})=\abs c. \] Hence no estimate \(\operatorname{dist}_1(T,\mathcal M)=O(\varepsilon(T)^\alpha)\), with \(\alpha>1/2\), can hold uniformly near the minimizer class in finite-dimensional determinant fibers.

label: lem:schatten-collapsed-multiplicities

title: Algebraic partitions are not unitary classes
label: rem:algebraic-partitions-not-unitary-classes
text_start: Jordan partitions classify finite-dimensional nilpotent root-space restrictions only up to algebraic similarity. They do not classify them up to unitary equivalence. For example, for \(t\ne0\) put \[ N_t=\begin{pmatrix}0&t\\0&0\end{pmatrix}. \] The matrices \(N_t\) and \(N_s\) have the same Jordan partition \((2)\) whenever \(s,t\ne0\). title: Riesz decomposition with quasinilpotent complement
label: lem:compact-riesz-root-space-quasinilpotent-complement
text_start: Let \(T\in\sone(H)\), and let \(F\subset\sigma(T)\setminus\{0\}\) be a finite set containing all non-zero spectral points of \(T\). title: Classical closure order inside the finite non-zero skeleton
label: thm:finite-support-quotient-closure-order
text_start: Assume the finite-support hypotheses of \Cref{thm:finite-support-quasinilpotent-quotient}. For \(\lambda\in\Sigma_{\mathcal D}\), let \(\pi_\lambda\) and \(\rho_\lambda\) be partitions of \(M_{\mathcal D}(\lambda)\), and let \(\mathcal O_\pi\) and \(\mathcal O_\rho\) be the corresponding finite-dimensional quotient strata, represented by determinant-fiber elements whose Jordan profiles at \(\lambda\) are respectively \(\pi_\lambda\) and \(\rho_\lambda\). label: cor:nonnormal-fiber-unbounded

label: cor:determinant-intrinsic-trace-budget
text_start: Let \(\mathcal D\) and \(\mathcal D'\) be summable cyclic data as in \Cref{thm:cyclic-data-classification}. title: Finite-dimensional specialization
label: rem:realisability-vs-rigidity
text_start: Let \(A\) be a finite matrix and let \(T\in \sone\) satisfy \[ \det(I-zT)=\det(I-zA). \] Then \(T\) and \(A\) have the same non-zero eigenvalues with algebraic multiplicity. Thus cyclic-block constructions may enlarge the ambient operator category, but they do not create spectral freedom once the determinant is prescribed. This is just \Cref{lem:fredholm-spectral-rigidity} applied to the finite-rank operator \(A\).
